newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel to forge ahead with Jerusalem settlement.
newsitem.headline: Israel to forge ahead with Jerusalem settlement.

text.p: Israel, rocked by the killing of seven schoolgirls by a Jordanian soldier, ignored world pleas to halt Jewish settlement plans in Arab East Jerusalem on Friday, vowing to send in the bulldozers soon.
The right-wing goverment of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu dismissed as "useless" a United Nations call to cancel the building of 6,500 homes between East Jerusalem and Bethelem.
Western and Arab leaders accuse Israel of endangering Middle East peacemaking and risking a violent Palestinian reaction by insisting on tightening its grip on Jerusalem.

"If anyone thinks the murder of little girls will bring this people to its knees...or that we will relinquish our birthright, holy land and eternal capital, he does not know the strength that exists in each person standing here around me today and in the entire nation," Netanyahu said at a funeral for four of the girls late on Thursday night.

The slaughter of the seven girls by a lone Jordanian soldier on Thursday diverted much of the international criticism Netanyahu has faced since his coalition government approved the building plan for the pine-covered hill called Jabal Abu Ghneim in Arabic or Har Homa in Hebrew.
"I am building Har Homa this week and nothing is going to stop me," Netanyahu said in an interview with the Maariv newspaper published on Friday.
"If they think they can frighten us, they are mistaken. I am determined about my view more than ever," he said.
Israeli officials said they expected work on the site to begin next Monday.
The U.N. General Assembly, by a vote of 130 to two, with two abstentions, called on Israel on Thursday to abandon the planned settlement.
The United States and Israel cast the only negative votes on the resolution, similar to one vetoed by the United States in the Security Council last Friday.
The Foreign Ministry rejected the resolution as "unilateral" and "useless".

Palestinian President Yasser Arafat went ahead on Friday with plans to receive U.S., European and Arab envoys in Gaza on Saturday to discuss Netanyahu's action which he believes could torpedo the entire U.S.-sponsored peace process.
Arafat, who had shunned contact with Netanyahu, said on Friday he would meet the Israeli leader to discuss settlement.
"If he is ready to implement the agreements, why not?" Arafat told reporters.
Jordan's King Hussein also accused Netanyahu this week of dragging regional peace to the abyss in a private letter which was leaked to the Israeli press.
The king was visibly shocked by the killing on Thursday. He said he wanted to visit the families of the girls, aged 12 to 13, killed at a border site nicknamed "The Island of Peace".
Netanyahu spokesman Shai Bazak told Reuters on Friday that Israel was checking the possibility of an Arafat meeting and a visit by King Hussein but "nothing has been set".
